blocks.en: Welcome back to Michael's Morning Listening!
Today we have two animal superstars for you: a fish that dresses up like a Muppet, and a giraffe that might be better at math than you are.
Let's dive in!
Have you ever seen a fish that looks like a character from Sesame Street?
Scientists have just given an official name to a very strange little fish — and they named it after Mr.
Snuffleupagus, Big Bird's big, shaggy best friend!
The fish is called Solenostomus snuffleupagus.
It is only about one and a half inches long — small enough to sit on your fingertip.
It is a type of ghost pipefish, a cousin of seahorses.
But this one is special: its whole body is covered in long, shaggy skin threads that look just like fur.
Put it next to a picture of Snuffleupagus, and you cannot unsee the resemblance!
Here is the cool part: those shaggy threads are not for keeping warm.
They are a disguise!
The fish lives on coral reefs, where red, hair-like algae floats in the water.
Its shaggy body looks exactly like that algae, so hungry hunters swim right past.
It is like wearing an invisibility cloak made of seaweed!
Scientists first photographed this fish more than twenty years ago.
It took them two whole decades of searching to prove it was a brand-new species.
Good things come to those who wait — even in science!
Now let's meet an animal famous for its long neck — but today we are going to talk about its brain instead.
At a zoo in Barcelona, Spain, scientists wanted to test whether giraffes can do math.
They showed four giraffes some boxes with carrots inside — a giraffe's favorite snack.
Here is how the game worked.
The scientist put carrots into two boxes where the giraffes could see them, then closed the boxes.
Next, he secretly moved more carrots into one of the closed boxes.
The giraffes could not see inside anymore.
Then he asked them to choose: which box has more carrots now?
To get it right, the giraffes had to remember the first amounts, then add the new carrots in their heads — without ever seeing the final pile.
And guess what?
They picked the right box about sixty-eight times out of a hundred — much better than random guessing!
Two giraffes, Nuru and Njano, were the star students.
But here is the twist: the giraffes were good at addition, but terrible at subtraction — exactly like most human kids!
So the next time math homework feels hard, remember: even a giraffe finds subtraction tricky.
This discovery is important because it shows that number skills are not just for humans, monkeys, and parrots.
The animal kingdom is full of secret mathematicians!
Here's today's idiom: "stick your neck out."
It means to take a risk, or to be brave enough to do something difficult.
For example: "She stuck her neck out and shared her idea in front of the whole class."
Just like a giraffe stretches its long neck to reach the highest leaves, when you stick your neck out, you reach for something that others are afraid to try!
That brings us to the end of today's show!

Before you go, here's a question: If you could have one superpower from any animal — camouflage like the ghost pipefish, or a giraffe's long neck — which would you choose, and what would you do with it?
Have a wonderful day, and see you tomorrow morning!
